findings.title: capability-tiers.tsx's TONE map is Record<string,string>, not Record<CapabilityLevel,string> -- no compile-time exhaustiveness when a level is added
findings.failure_scenario: CapabilityLevel (document-state.ts) is the closed set this map is meant to mirror, and it is exported. Because TONE is keyed by the widened but still-generic string type, TypeScript raises nothing when a level is missing from the map -- exactly the situation this commit was in a moment before it added the `proposal_only` line by hand. A future sixth level (or a rename of an existing one) can land in CapabilityLevel/CAPABILITY_LEVELS without the compiler ever flagging that TONE has fallen out of sync; the only symptom is a silently unstyled badge (`tierTone` falls through to `""`), caught only if someone happens to look at the rendered page or writes a component test -- and the ticket's own report says explicitly that no component test exists for this file for ANY of its five levels today.
findings.required_fix: Type TONE as `Record<CapabilityLevel, string>` (or build it via a `satisfies Record<CapabilityLevel, string>` object) so the compiler enforces the map is exhaustive over the same closed set `CapabilityLevel` already names, the same way `isCapabilityLevel`/`CAPABILITY_LEVELS` already treat that set as closed. This is a design deepening, not a behavior change for this ticket, and was true before #988 touched this file -- #988 had the map open for editing and extended the existing pattern rather than hardening it. Judgement call, not a hard violation: nothing in this repo's documented standards mandates it, and the smell (a documented repo standard) can be waived by the next editor of this file.
